extracted.intended_audience: performers, improv teams, comedy creators, and UCB community members interested in submitting to Del Close Marathon (DCM22)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for submitting shows and programming pitches to the Del Close Marathon (DCM22) in New York, including acceptable formats, slot lengths, deadlines, fees, and waiver information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key dates and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: February 2 - DCM22 submissions open. February 28 - DCM22 submissions close. April 1 - Programming and schedule announcements released. Week of June 8 - Workshops and special programming begins. June 12 through 14 - DCM22 Festival takes place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit within the February 2–28 window; programming announcements and workshops follow the stated timeline leading up to the festival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness / eligibility to apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are open to the public, and we invite all to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anyone may apply, though there are special notes for current Harold teams: Current Harold teams on both coasts need not submit — you'll be contacted directly regarding your participation. House team members wishing to submit a different team or show should submit via the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted show types and slot lengths
rubrics_metrics.description: This year submissions can take the form of: An improv team seeking a 15-30 minute slot. An improv show format that improv teams can be booked into, seeking a 30 or 60 minute slot (eg. Play by Play, Cagematch). A late night bit show pitch seeking a 15 minute slot. A non-improv show or alternative programming pitch, seeking a 30 or 60 minute slot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be clear in your submission which category and slot length you're requesting; example formats are given for guidance. Non-improv/alternative programming is permitted but is not the primary focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Festival focus / selection priority
rubrics_metrics.description: DCM will always be about improv first and foremost. But as UCB's curriculum and programming expand, this year we're also allowing non-improv shows and alternative programming to submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect selection to prioritize improv work; non-improv submissions are allowed but 'will not be the focus of the festival.' Use the opportunity to connect with the broader UCB/improv/comedy community, but selection likelihood may favor improv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission fee and fee structure
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be a $15 fee per submission ($5 for late night bit show submissions) this year to help address costs associated with the programming committee, submission reviews, and other logistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan to pay the applicable fee when submitting; the lower fee applies specifically to late night bit show submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee waiver eligibility and process
rubrics_metrics.description: If the submission fee is not financially feasible for you, you’ll be able to request a waiver. Currently enrolled UCB students, and active college students/teams will also be able to request a waiver. Instructions on how to do so will be provided via the submission form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request a waiver via the submission form if needed; UCB students and active college teams are explicitly noted as eligible to request waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit / submission form
rubrics_metrics.description: The form is available here: https://ucbcomedy.com/dcm-22-submissions/
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All submissions should be made through the provided online form; waiver instructions and any additional submission details will be on that form.
